entity: United States Department of Agriculture - Forest Service
role: Federal agency, commenter on environmental impact
stance_basis: letter recommending specific vegetation and drainage measures as conditions for acceptable environmental impact
summary: The United States Department of Agriculture - Forest Service submitted a letter dated September 20, 1974, commenting on the Lincoln Highway improvement project. The agency expressed interest in the effect on woodland and vegetation, recommending trees and shrubs in the median strip for soil retention, traffic distraction prevention, and noise barriers, and requesting a description of tree losses from right-of-way widening. The agency also flagged a potential drainage concern at the western section of the route.
complaint_summary: The Forest Service recommended planting trees and shrubs in the median strip for soil retention, traffic distraction prevention, and noise barriers; requested a description of tree losses from right-of-way widening; and noted a potential water drainage problem at the western section of the route.

statement.text:
We have reviewed the Mobility Studies description for Section 4(f) lands - F.A. Route 23 (U.S. Route 30), Lincoln Highway (Chicago Avenue to Cicero Avenue) Cook County, Illinois.
Our interest in the project is in the effect on woodland and other vegetation, and largely coincides with that of the Cook County Forest Preserve District, with whom you have been working. A few trees and shrubs in the median strip would hold the soil and also prevent distraction between eastbound and westbound traffic. Trees can also be used as a noise barrier where needed.
According to the document, most of the route will be through business and residential property. The residential properties, at least, undoubtedly have some trees. A description of the losses of trees, resulting from the increase of the width of the right of way, would facilitate evaluation of environmental impact.
Some water may be trapped behind the slight slopes on both sides of the road at the western section (Exhibit "B") unless provisions are made for drainage of the low spots.
Thank you for the opportunity to comment on this highway project.
Sincerely,
Assistant Director
Environmental Protection & Improvement
